urls.description: Large language models increasingly write the code behind empirical research. This column reports a benchmark of 40 econometric tasks in Stata, R, and Python. For each task, two leading models write a script, as a chatbot that never runs it and as an agent that runs and revises it. Letting the models run their code raises the share of correct results from 79% to 97% and makes the prompt and the software matter far less. The failures that remain under the agent come from scripts that run without errors but return wrong numbers, and detecting them is still the researcher’s work.
urls.title: Letting AI agents write econometric code

“Yet risks lurk behind the glory,” Yan said. On the one hand, the photovoltaic industry has entered a period of deep adjustment. On the other, some foreign countries are using trade barriers and localization policies to force Chinese companies building factories overseas to confront harsh requirements, including sharing core technologies and being denied controlling ownership. Such conduct not only threatens companies’ profit margins, but could also allow the generational lead that China built through immense hardship to be “scooped up on the cheap.”

“然而，辉煌背后暗藏风险。”严大洲说，一方面，光伏行业进入深度调整期；另一方面，部分海外国家通过贸易壁垒和本地化政策，倒逼我国企业在海外建厂时面临核心技术共享、不得控股等苛刻要求。这种行为不仅威胁到企业的利润空间，更可能导致我国历经千辛万苦建立起的代际领先优势被“弯道抄底”。

Yan believes that imposing export controls on core technologies is precisely intended to add a “safety catch” to China’s strategic energy security. It clearly draws a “red line” against technology outflows, ensuring that core processes representing national competitiveness—such as key technologies, equipment, drawings, algorithms and process packages—are not lost through disorderly competition or abnormal commercial conduct. This is a strategic move to safeguard national economic security and the global pattern of industrial competition.

urls.description: We revisit well-established mechanisms for primordial black hole (PBH) production, namely inflation, phase transitions, and cosmic strings, in the context of the dark dimension scenario, which is motivated by swampland principles. Applying quantum gravity constraints, we demonstrate that any viable mechanism, barring exotic new physics at low energies, inevitably leads to the formation of five-dimensional PBHs. We further show that PBHs formed from cosmic strings can have lifetimes comparable to the age of the Universe. We comment on the observational implications of this result, including a potential connection to the recent detection of a high-energy neutrino by KM3NeT, whose energy is intriguingly close to the five-dimensional Planck scale in the dark dimension scenario.

When President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy diesel from Russia, “it was easy to shrug off the move as a feeble effort to limit energy prices in advance of the midterms,” writes expert Stephen Sestanovich.

The story now looks "disturbingly different; the possible consequences, much more serious, and likely to last well beyond the midterms."

A day after announcing new diesel imports from Russia, Trump began calling for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s removal from office. He followed this up by claiming that Moscow and Kyiv had agreed to suspend attacks on each other’s main energy targets.

"This, it quickly became clear, was pure invention. Reports suggested what had actually happened was that U.S. negotiators were pressing the Ukrainian government to do something far more radical than a mutual ceasefire—to cease its attacks unilaterally, whether Russia complied or not," Sestanovich writes.

“It is hard to overstate how much this new public hostility by U.S. officials—above all, the president—has disoriented Ukraine’s leadership,” he writes. “In searching for a new way to handle Trump, Ukraine’s leadership has seemed suddenly at sea."

"Rather than see the prospect of postwar riches as the key that will bring Putin to the table, he now acts as though pressure—on Zelenskyy, not Putin—will be the crucial instrument of a breakthrough,” Sestanovich argues.

note_tweet.text:
Cyber-enabled scams are spreading globally with the aid of emerging technologies like AI.

In Southeast Asia, criminal networks are using AI to traffic individuals into scam centers and leveraging the technology to deceive fraud victims.

CFR expert Rita Fernández conducted field research in Thailand to learn how AI is used to enable human trafficking. She spoke with law enforcement, civil society, and government officials.

"Conditions in the scam compounds are harrowing," she writes. "Victims are stripped of their passports and belongings, threatened, beaten, and tortured."

"Some are told they need to work to repay travel expenses they incurred and to regain access to their passports. If they resist working, or fail to meet quotas, they may be denied food or subjected to psychological abuse, leaving them with no choice but to comply."

“AI is not limited to use in cyber scams and human trafficking—law enforcement has seen a steady increase in broader AI use in crime."

"Just as individuals can use AI to become more productive at work and in the classroom, criminal networks can use it to improve their efficiency as well," one source told Fernández.

Some impressions from the Bank-Fund meetings in Bangkok:

1. The words are all negative but the numbers are all positive. Is all about unprecedented waves of shocks and risks while the IMF upgraded the forecast to something even stronger.

2. No one cares about tariffs anymore, they expect them to continue forever and have adjusted and moved on.

3. Everyone cares a lot about high interest rates. They expect them to continue forever but they haven't moved on.

4. Oil prices fall somewhere between these two. Everyone cares some, aren't sure if they'll continue and have partially moved on.

5. Everyone is having exactly the same conversations about AI as they are having here: will the demand boost continue, is it a bubble, will it kill jobs, when will it show up in productivity. I sensed much more optimism than pessimism and finance ministers and central bankers are not particuarly interested in p(doom).

6. No one seemed to mind that Scott Bessent didn't bother to attend.
